jobs.description:
Are you an experienced forklift driver with warehouse and order-picking experience? We are looking for a reliable and dedicated forklift operator for a full-time position in Lynge, with the possibility of an immediate start.

You will become part of a dedicated warehouse team, where your primary responsibilities will include forklift driving, order picking, and general warehouse tasks. The position is ideal for someone who enjoys physical work, thrives in a busy environment, and takes pride in ensuring efficient and well-organized warehouse operations.

Job Responsibilities:

• 
Operating forklifts in connection with warehouse operations

• 
Picking orders for customers

• 
Order picking using a Pick by Voice system

• 
Receiving and sorting incoming goods

• 
Maintaining order and organization in the warehouse

The position offers a varied workday with a combination of routine and diverse tasks. Your contribution will play an important role in ensuring smooth and efficient warehouse operations. Experience with Pick by Voice systems is an advantage.

Working Hours:

This is a full-time position, Monday to Friday.

• 
Monday–Thursday: 07:00–15:15

• 
Friday: 07:00–14:45

Starting date is preferably Monday the 16th or Tuesday the 17th of November.

The position is until the end of the year with the possibility of being extended.

We Are Looking for Someone Who:

• 
Holds a valid Danish forklift certificate

• 
Has at least 2 months of forklift driving experience

• 
Has previous warehouse experience, preferably with order picking

• 
Has experience with Pick by Voice systems (an advantage)

• 
Is reliable, flexible, and able to work independently

• 
Enjoys working as part of a team

• 
Can speak and understand English at a good level

What We Offer:

You will receive a thorough introduction and training to ensure you have the best possible start and the tools needed to succeed in the role.

The workplace is characterized by strong team spirit, an informal atmosphere, and a focus on safety, well-being, and collaboration.

The salary is determined in accordance with the Industry Collective Agreement and is 159.50 DKK per hour, including holiday allowance and flexible benefits.

Does this sound like the right opportunity for you? Send us your application as soon as possible. We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will hire candidates as soon as the right profiles are identified.

If you have any questions about the position, please feel free to contact us at +45 60 10 30 70.

Please note that ID verification, a criminal record check, and reference checks are part of the recruitment process.

**Student Analyst in Strategy & Transformation

**

**Who We Are

**

NNIT is a niche specialist in IT for life sciences and highly regulated industries. We help pharma, biotech and medtech companies across Europe, the US and Asia, as well as public sector and regulated customers in Denmark, solve their most complex challenges where technology, regulation and business critical processes meet.

We are in the middle of a fundamental transformation. Our strategy, OneNNIT 2030, sets out how we will sharpen our position as a niche specialist, reshape our portfolio into a focused set of value pathways that take customers from advisory through implementation to managed services, bring our US and European organisations together as one, and become a genuinely AI-driven company.

The Strategy & Transformation Office leads that journey. It reports directly to our CEO, owns NNIT's strategy cycle, runs the transformation programme and builds the capabilities that will carry the momentum through to 2030. We are now building the team, and we are looking for a Student Analyst who wants to work at the heart of it.

**What You Will Do

**

This is not a back-office student job. You will work on the same questions as our CEO and Executive Management, and you will see first-hand how strategy is set, decided and turned into action in a listed company.

You do not need to be a technical AI specialist. You should, however, care deeply about how AI reshapes organisations, ways of working and business models, because that question runs through everything we do.

**Typical tasks include

**

• Supporting the programme management of OneNNIT 2030, from planning and milestone tracking to following up on decisions across the organisation

• Preparing sharp decision material, presentations and updates for the CEO, Executive Management and the Board

• Analysing our offerings, markets and competitors as we shape the value pathways NNIT will take to market

• Supporting the annual strategy cycle and strategic projects, including the screening and assessment of partnerships and acquisitions

• Helping drive NNIT's journey to becoming an AI-driven company, across our offerings, our delivery model and our internal ways of working

• Contributing to the change management and internal communication that help colleagues understand and own the transformation

• Preparing and facilitating workshops and leadership meetings

**What You Will Bring

**

We imagine that you

• Are preferably in the third year of your Bachelor's degree, or in the first year of your Master’s degree, for example in Strategy, Organisation and Leadership at Copenhagen Business School

• Have a strong interest in strategy, transformation, change management and AI

• Are analytical and structured, and able to turn complex input into clear, well-argued recommendations

• Write well and build presentations that make their point quickly

• Have strong Excel and PowerPoint skills and are comfortable with the rest of Microsoft Office and everyday AI tools

• Communicate clearly and professionally in English, both written and spoken

• Take initiative, challenge your own thinking, handle confidential information with discretion and enjoy working with senior stakeholders

**What We Offer

**

You will join the Strategy & Transformation Office, which reports directly to the CEO, and work closely with the Head of Strategy & Transformation. You will have a front-row seat as NNIT redefines its strategy, organisation and portfolio, and you will work alongside Executive Management, senior leaders across Europe, the US and Asia, and our external advisors.

You will get real responsibility from day one, high exposure to senior leadership and the flexibility to balance work with your studies. Few student jobs offer a closer view of how strategy and transformation are done in practice.

**Practical Information

**

The role is 15 to 20 hours per week, with flexibility around exams.

Please upload your CV and cover letter in English. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply soon.

About NNIT

NNIT is a publicly listed company that specializes in IT solutions to life sciences internationally, and to the public and enterprise sectors in Denmark. We focus on high complexity industries and thrive in environments where regulatory demands and complexity are high. We advise on and build sustainable digital solutions that work for the patients, citizens, employees, end users or customers.

NNIT consists of group company NNIT A/S and subsidiaries SCALES, Excellis Health Solutions and SL Controls. Together, these companies employ more than 1,600 people in Europe, Asia, and USA.

We celebrate diversity and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees. We actively work to eliminate bias and ensure an inclusive workplace where everyone has the right to be seen and heard as they are. We invite interested candidates to apply, no matter their background.

In the interest of fostering a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request candidates to refrain from including their pictures in their applications.

Senior Engineer – AI & Data Products (Aarhus)

The Tech Collective, Data & AI

Kalkværksvej 5, 8000 Aarhus · Full-time

We’re looking for a senior builder who turns AI and data into products people actually use. You’ve shipped real systems end to end, you know AI or data well enough to make it work in production, not just in a demo, and AI is as much a part of how you build as what you build.

What you'll do

In this role, you’ll take client ideas from a rough hypothesis to a working prototype, and then to a production system that runs reliably. You'll design the architecture, write the code across frontend, backend, and data, and decide what to build and what to leave out. It's a hands-on role. Most of your time goes into building, and the rest goes into working with clients to make sure you’re building the right thing.

The work covers generative AI applications and agents, including the harnesses that make them reliable (tools, context, memory, orchestration, and guardrails), along with retrieval pipelines and the data flows they depend on. You’ll connect these to client systems, deploy them in the cloud, and set up the evals and observability you need to see whether they work and how to improve them. You’ll work closely with our data platform and AI specialists, review code, and help less experienced engineers grow.

What you'll bring

You're a builder at heart. You have a master's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, (preferably) 5+ years of hands-on software experience, and a track record of shipping production-ready software systems. Ideally, you also have experience with the whole software development lifecycle: starting with an idea (whether your own or a stakeholder’s), designing the solution architecture, developing and testing the solution, and putting it into the hands of actual users. Good engineering matters to you, but you’re not a purist, you care more about shipping something that works and solves the problem.

What sets you apart is depth beyond the code. You know AI (LLMs, agents, RAG, evals) and data (data modelling, pipelines, event-driven, and real-time systems) well enough that others come to you for it. Ideally, you know a bit of both.

You're equally at home building AI products and building with AI. Coding agents and AI-assisted tools are part of how you work every day, and you use them critically. You know where they make you faster and where the output needs a careful human eye.

To be a great fit, it helps if you have:

• 
Solid full-stack skills in Python and/or TypeScript (e.g., React, Next.js, FastAPI), with production systems to show for it

• 
Hands-on experience building agents and the harnesses around them (tool use, MCP, context and memory management, orchestration, guardrails), and designing the data models and pipelines that real products run on

• 
An AI-native way of working, using coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex in your own development workflow, with a clear view of where they help and where they don’t

• 
Experience deploying and running solutions on AWS, Azure, or GCP, including containers, CI/CD, and enough observability to know what's going on

• 
System-level judgement: you can reason about architecture, trade-offs, and failure modes, and you can spot the weak points in an existing stack

• 
Curiosity about the client’s problem, and the ability to explain technical choices clearly to people who don’t write code

• 
A habit of helping others get better through sparring, pairing, and code reviews

English is our corporate language. Proficiency in one or more additional languages is a plus.

What we offer

At The Tech Collective, you’ll join a team of 30 consultants that feels closer to a nerdy startup than a large consultancy, while being firmly backed by Implement Consulting Group. You’ll own what you build, and you’ll have the freedom to shape your role in the direction that motivates you.

You’ll work on data and AI problems across industries, alongside experienced peers in AI, data, and software. Our culture is built on trust, curiosity, humility, and impact, with high autonomy, co-creation, and active knowledge-sharing.

Ready to build with us? We review applications on an ongoing basis, so apply as soon as you can.

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about driving operational excellence, improving business performance, and enabling retail teams to deliver outstanding results? Then we might have just the job for you at Specsavers.

Join Specsavers as our new Senior Store Operations & Retail Delivery Manager and play a key role in shaping operational performance, supporting retail transformation initiatives, and driving sustainable growth across Northern Europe.

Your role

As our Senior Store Operations & Retail Delivery Manager, you will be responsible for supporting the execution of strategic initiatives, operational plans, and performance improvement programmes across our Northern Europe retail business.

Working closely with the Director of Stores, Heads of Stores, Business Performance Managers, and Regional Relationship Managers, you will help create the conditions for stores to improve profitability, strengthen operational excellence, and deliver outstanding customer experiences.

You will act as a key link between regional field teams, support functions, and business leaders, ensuring that the right tools, frameworks, and initiatives are in place to support long-term business success. You are a strong collaborator who thrives in complex environments, enjoys working across functions, and is motivated by helping others achieve measurable business results.

Finally, you are ready an everyday where you combine working from home with being at the Northern European Support Office in Copenhagen along with frequent visits to the countries in the region.

Key responsibilities include:

• Driving business improvement and performance programmes across multiple markets.

• Identifying opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and operational performance.

• Supporting strategic planning and execution together with regional and country stakeholders.

• Ensuring retail tools, processes, and initiatives are effectively implemented and continuously improved.

• Building strong partnerships across functions to deliver sustainable business outcomes.

Your new team

You'll join the Northern Europe Store Operations function and work closely with senior retail leaders, business performance specialists, regional relationship managers, and a broad range of support functions.

The team plays an important role in supporting our store network, helping country teams deliver sustainable growth, operational excellence, and outstanding customer experiences.

As part of an international and highly collaborative environment, you'll contribute to projects and initiatives that directly influence business performance across multiple markets.

What are we looking for?

We are preferably looking for a candidate with the following competencies:

• Strong experience in retail operations, business performance, or operational excellence.

• Experience from a similar role or i.e. a Regional Relationship Manager role

• Commercial and financial acumen, including business planning and performance analysis.

• Experience leading cross-functional projects and driving measurable business improvements.

• Working with operating and supporting teams individually and remotely

• Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills.

• A data-driven and analytical approach to solving business challenges.

It would be an advantage if you have:

• Leadership experience working in franchise, partnership, or multi-site retail environments.

• Experience across multiple markets or countries.

• Knowledge of business transformation, change management, or performance improvement programmes.

• Experience using Power BI or similar reporting tools.

As a person, we believe that you are:

• Commercially minded and focused on creating results.

• A strong collaborator who builds trust and alignment across teams.

• Structured, proactive, and comfortable managing complexity.

• An engaging communicator who can influence stakeholders at all levels.

What awaits you upon joining Specsavers

At Specsavers, you'll get more than just a job. You will join us on a journey to make eye health and hearing services accessible to everyone.

We offer an exciting and challenging role in an organisation with strong ambitions, where you'll be part of a collaborative and supportive culture.

Joining us, you’ll get:

• Competitive compensation and benefits.

• Professional and personal development opportunities.

• A collaborative and inclusive culture.

• The opportunity to influence business performance across multiple countries.

• Exposure to senior stakeholders and strategic initiatives within an international organisation.

Is this your next step? Then apply today

To apply, please send us your CV using the button below. We want to respect your time, so including an application letter is optional. Feel free to apply as soon as possible. Please avoid including any photos or references to your age in your CV. It contributes to a fairer and more unbiased assessment.

We review CVs and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis. Our recruitment process typically consists of an initial screening, two rounds of interviews, and a personality assessment feedback session.

If you have any questions regarding the role, please contact the hiring manager Jacob Vejen by e-mail: jacob.vejen@specsavers.com.

Diversity & Inclusion at Specsavers

Specsavers will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other legally protected factor.

In line with our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, we integrate these principles into all aspects of our work, from product development to team building.

jobs.description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We're looking for an interim In-house Legal Counsel to join our Legal team at Pleo in Copenhagen, Denmark. In this role, you'll serve as a trusted legal advisor across the business, protecting our interests and enabling growth as we scale our fintech platform. If you're excited about working at the intersection of legal strategy and operational excellence, and are passionate about building a compliant, well-governed fintech company, then this is the opportunity for you!

What you’ll be doing

As an In-house Legal Counsel, you will:

• 
Serve as the primary point of contact for business queries across all departments, providing timely, practical legal guidance on day-to-day operational matters.

• 
Support our People team on employment law, workplace policies, and labor compliance, including contract reviews, policy drafting, and regulatory adherence across multiple jurisdictions.

• 
Corporate administration by drafting, reviewing, and amending internal policies, procedures, and standardised legal templates that the business can use efficiently.

• 
Assist managing fraud and compliance escalations by conducting liability assessments, performing compliance checks, and providing risk mitigation advice to protect the business.

• 
Assist with customer disputes and regulatory engagement with the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS), supporting escalations, preparing responses, and helping to ensure we meet all regulatory deadlines and requirements.

What you bring

You'll thrive in this role if you have:

• 
A Cand.Jur or equivalent legal qualification recognised in Denmark.

• 
2-5 years of legal experience – ideally in fintech, financial services, or a fast-growing scale-up environment where you've handled a broad range of matters.

• 
Knowledge about employment law and HR compliance – you understand the nuances of employment contracts, workplace policies, and labor law across multiple jurisdictions.

• 
Strong vendor and contract management skills – you can review, negotiate, and draft commercial agreements efficiently.

• 
Excellent communication skills – you can translate complex legal concepts into practical business advice for non-legal stakeholders.

• 
A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset – you see problems as opportunities and can manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• 
Experience with compliance and risk management in a regulated industry is a plus as well as managing regulatory escalations and disputes, particularly with financial regulators or ombudsman services.

•

• 
You want genuine input into decisions, balancing the technically correct answer against what actually works commercially

•

This role is not a good fit for you if:

•

•

•

• 
Get to know the business well enough that your advice fits how Pleo actually operates, not just what the regulation says

• 
Start shaping the policies and templates the move from startup to corporate needs

Department: Enterprise IT & Quality

Location: Greater Copenhagen Area/ Ballerup /Denmark

As a Data Governance Professional, you will help shape how Novo and Enterprise IT put privacy and AI compliance requirements into practice. You will combine policy development with hands-on operational support, working across data governance with a strong focus on privacy, the responsible use of AI and data science, and their links to information security.

You will take ownership of maintaining and developing privacy requirements, controls and supporting guidance for IT solutions. Working directly with IT teams and data owners, you will help translate these requirements into workable solutions and carry improvements through to implementation. As Lead Data Ethics Responsible (DER) for Enterprise IT, you will also coordinate local privacy and AI compliance activities and drive our DER network.

You will work alongside experienced colleagues who provide professional guidance and specialist support. You will bring curiosity about technology, analytical thinking and the drive to move work forward, taking increasing responsibility and working more independently as your expertise grows.

Your new role

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Maintaining and developing privacy requirements, controls and guidance for IT solutions, translating regulatory and internal requirements into practical expectations across the IT and data lifecycle.

• Working with relevant specialists and process owners to keep this content current, address gaps and agree changes through the relevant governance processes.

• Providing practical support to IT teams and data owners on privacy and AI compliance, including documenting processing activities, supporting risk and impact assessments, and following up on agreed actions.

• Acting as Lead DER for Enterprise IT, driving and maintaining our local DER network, coordinating shared activities and helping colleagues carry out their responsibilities.

• Contributing to policies and frameworks covering privacy, AI and data science, and information security, in collaboration with stakeholders across Novo.

• Helping shape and deliver projects that improve how we manage, use and protect data, including simplifying compliance processes and supporting implementation of requirements and controls.

• Developing and delivering guidance, training and communication that make requirements easier to understand and apply.

You will have a defined area of responsibility, with specialist support and clear routes for decisions and escalation on complex matters.

Your new department

IT Process & Compliance defines, governs and continuously improves fit-for-purpose IT and data processes. We help the organisation meet regulatory expectations and provide insight and practical partnering to strengthen compliance across Novo.

Our work covers process management, compliance awareness and partnering, and support for audits and inspections. We also drive the privacy agenda across Enterprise IT, helping the organisation protect personal information and meet data protection requirements.

We work closely with stakeholders across Novo to turn requirements and identified issues into practical improvements. You will join colleagues with different professional backgrounds who work together across policy development, operational compliance and project delivery.

Your skills & qualifications

You are at the beginning of your career and want to develop at the intersection of governance, compliance and technology. You may be a recent graduate or have some relevant experience from employment, a student position, an internship or project work.

We are looking for someone who brings:

• A relevant degree, for example in law, IT, digital governance, data science or business, or equivalent relevant experience.

• A foundation or interest in privacy and data protection, gained through study or practical experience, and an interest in AI governance, data governance and information security.

• Curiosity about how IT solutions, AI and data science work, including how data is collected, used, shared and retained.

• An analytical approach and the ability to translate complex information into clear explanations and practical actions.

• Good collaboration skills and the confidence to ask questions, seek input and follow up with stakeholders.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

You enjoy both analysing a problem and completing the work needed to solve it. You organise your tasks, take responsibility for agreed deliverables and recognise when specialist input is needed. You look for ways to make compliance simpler and more effective.

We do not expect you to be a specialist in every area. We expect you to bring a relevant foundation, sound judgement and a willingness to learn.

What you’ll do

• Partner with Consumer Care and regional teams to understand what success looks like for consumer engagement, and turn it into practical analytics and reporting.

Working across functions and markets gives you the opportunity to build new skills, broaden your perspective and see your work adopted by teams who rely on it.

Outsourcing Project Director - Drug Substance Outsourcing

Category:  Project Management & Agile

Location:

Høje-Taastrup, Capital Region of Denmark, DK

Your impact begins here

As Project Director, you will lead the most complex sourcing projects in Drug Substance, from category strategy through to signed contracts with CMOs, where commitments can exceed DKK 1 billion. You will shape strategies for areas of growing importance to Novo, such as synthetic peptides, and negotiate partnerships that are strong commercially and sustainable over time. Your work helps keep the supply of treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases reliable.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior sourcing and project leader who combines a strategic mindset with an eye for contractual detail.

You have:

• A university master’s degree in pharmacy, biology, engineering, supply chain management, law or business.

• Around 15+ years of relevant pharmaceutical experience, in manufacturing, manufacturing development and/or CMO environments. The role may suit candidates with around 20 years of experience.

• A strong background in strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and external partner management.

• Solid experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, as project and/or line manager.

• In-depth knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing, CMOs, quality and regulatory requirements.

• Excellent negotiation and contracting skills, and the ability to engage with senior management and CMO executives, up to CEO level.

• The ability to lead and influence without formal authority, with resilience, autonomy, a sense of urgency and strong execution skills.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Supplementary training in areas such as cGMP, project execution or personal development.

• An existing network within Novo, CMOs and pharmaceutical engineering companies.

• Experience in Drug Product sourcing.

What you’ll do

You will own sourcing projects from the first idea to final implementation, and you will keep strategy, contract and delivery pointing in the same direction.

In practice, you will:

• Develop category strategies for areas of strategic importance, such as synthetic peptides, by pairing market insight, including global players and trends, with Novo’s strategic outlook.

• Lead critical CMO negotiations independently until signature, securing outcomes within mandate that balance value, cost, flexibility, speed and risk.

• Drive projects end-to-end: set up governance and Steering Committees, build business cases and plans, define deliverables and manage risk.

• Bring together specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Finance and Legal, and raise bottlenecks early so work keeps moving.

• Keep SVP and EVP-level stakeholders informed and aligned on progress, and give input to business plans and budgets.

• Raise the standard for how Drug Substance Outsourcing works by sharing your approach with category managers and developing sourcing standards.

Who you’ll work with

You will be a senior individual contributor in GSOD Drug Substance Outsourcing, reporting to the Senior Director of the department. The role has no direct reports, but you will lead through influence: category groups and project teams with specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Finance and Legal, as well as colleagues in Global Contract Manufacturing DS, Supply Chain Design, GMS Management and country affiliates.

Externally, you will work with CMOs across the US, Europe and Asia, so you should expect to spend significant time abroad. You will balance partnership and long-term collaboration with the best possible commercial terms for Novo, and you will be at ease handling cross-cultural discussions when tension runs high.

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes, devices and products for the people who need them. Your primary focus will be Drug Substance, with potential involvement in Drug Product and Devices.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take decisions independently and to give strategic guidance to senior leaders on the project portfolio. You will build new skills through cross-functional and cross-border work, and you will be recognised for results through clear performance expectations.

You will also have room to challenge convention: to find faster, better ways to run projects and to shape new processes and standards for CMO partnerships.

The pay range for this role is 940,800 – 1,448,700 DKK per year. The final offer reflects your experience and qualifications.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead Novo’s most strategic CMO partnerships from strategy to signature, apply for the Project Director role by 19st November 2026 . We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Uffe Holme ufho@novonordisk.com

Health and Safety Supporter

Department: API LP – HSE & Infrastructure

Location: Kalundborg, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Health and Safety Supporter, you will help create a safe working environment as projects and operations move forward at API LP Kalundborg. You will drive safety improvements, support risk assessments, inspections and incident follow-up, and help ensure that our work complies with Danish legislation, Novo Nordisk requirements and our ISO 45001-aligned management system. Your work will protect colleagues and contractors every day while enabling projects and operations to progress safely.

What you’ll bring

You combine a technical understanding of production with a practical and structured approach to health and safety. You are comfortable working independently while building strong relationships across projects, operations and external partners.

To succeed in this role, you bring:

• 
A technical background, for example as a production or process technician, or a relevant technical academic education.

• 
Professional-level Danish and English, both spoken and written.

• 
Familiarity with management systems such as ISO 45001 and experience of, or familiarity with, project management.

• 
Experience working across functions and the ability to influence stakeholders without formal authority.

• 
Statutory Working Environment training for Health & Safety Representatives and relevant company or health and safety training, such as fire safety, first aid or workplace assessment courses.

• 
A proactive, credible and solution-oriented approach, supported by strong communication skills.

It would be useful, but is not essential, if you have an education within health and safety or two to five years of experience in health and safety management, ideally in an operational or project-based environment.

• Knowledge of Danish health and safety legislation, compliance requirements, risk assessments or accident and incident investigations would also be an advantage.

What you’ll do

As the day-to-day health and safety support for projects and operations at API LP Kalundborg, you will take initiative and help teams continuously improve the way they work safely.

• 
Drive safety improvements throughout project execution and operational readiness, promoting a safety-first and LEAN mindset.

• 
Carry out planned Health, Safety and Environment line walks and safety inspections and provide daily health and safety follow-up, including the processing and follow-up of incidents and near-misses.

• 
Support risk assessments, including assessments involving hazardous media, and contribute to relevant EHS Portal activities.

• 
Support work permits, including GMO-related permits where relevant, as well as Work Wise, emergency response and inspection readiness.

• 
Support the Health & Safety Representative organisation, helping ensure that employee representatives are involved in decisions affecting the working environment.

• 
Support training and introductions and share good health and safety practices across teams and contractors.

Who you’ll work with

You will join API LP – HSE & Infrastructure in Global Manufacturing & Supply and be based at API LP Kalundborg, which will be the scope of your responsibility.

You will collaborate with project managers, people managers in API, Environment, Health and Safety coordinators and colleagues, Health & Safety Partners and Health & Safety Representatives. Externally, you will work with NNE, project subcontractors and consultants.

You will bring these perspectives together, speak up when progress stalls and help teams reach clear, safe decisions at pace.

What you can expect here

You will have a high degree of independence and the trust to use it. You will be supported to perform at your best, encouraged to make your voice heard and given opportunities to contribute your expertise. Working across projects, operations and a broad network of partners will give you opportunities to build new skills and broaden your understanding of the value chain.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 499,600 to 734,400 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to make safe work the standard across API LP Kalundborg, apply for the Health and Safety Supporter role by 15 November 2026.

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible via the link.

For questions, please reach out to Martin Winther Wulff, Mww@novonordisk.com.

As Senior Process Engineer, Cleaning, you will keep cleaning processes in API manufacturing stable, validated and continuously improving. You will use data and process science to find root causes, make the case for improvements that matter, and help colleagues grow into subject matter experts. Your work protects product quality in Kalundborg, so more people living with serious chronic diseases can rely on their treatment every day.

What you’ll bring

You are systematic, curious about the science behind a clean process and comfortable taking ownership. You bring:

• A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a relevant scientific or technical discipline.

• 6+ years of experience within cleaning in pharmaceutical or API manufacturing.

• The ability to independently understand the scientific principles behind cleaning, including how chemistry and equipment interact.

• Experience working independently with cleaning validation and process optimisation.

• Strong GMP knowledge and good documentation practice according to cGMP.

• The ability to monitor data, extract insight from it and recommend actionable alternatives, with an appetite for analytical methods.

• The ability to explain complex information to different audiences and bring people on board.

• A quality mindset, respectful teamwork and the independence to make sound decisions.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience with equipment qualification and process validation (IQ, OQ, PV).

• Experience coaching colleagues or contributing to inspections.

What you’ll do

You will be a driving force for cleaning process understanding in your area, turning data and experience into stable, compliant and continuously improved processes.

• Support daily process execution and troubleshooting, using systematic problem solving to find root causes and drive continuous improvement.

• Use data to visualise, analyse and explain process performance, and drive standardisation of tasks, data collection and analysis.

• Build scientific understanding of the process, linking it to product quality and recommending optimisation projects, with a clear justification for each.

• Develop and perform process confirmation, and grow your responsibility for cleaning validation and other types of process qualification and validation.

• Develop colleagues with more than two years’ experience into subject matter experts, keeping an ongoing dialogue on their individual development plans.

• Keep your area inspection-ready, take part in inspections and share best practice with colleagues across API.

Who you’ll work with

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes and products for the people who need them. You will join API IO M3 Process Support in Kalundborg, Denmark, reporting to [insert hiring manager name and title].

Every day you will work closely with colleagues in your own department, including Associate Managers, Quality Coordinators, administrative employees and team members. You will also collaborate with other departments across the area to secure good collaboration, systematic problem solving and timely product delivery.

You will share knowledge across API manufacturing facilities, forums and process groups, and communicate results to managers and department managers, and at times to senior leaders within API. Together, you will keep priorities clear and move forward with urgency.

What you can expect here

You will have a high degree of independence within your area, and we expect you to challenge current practices and take initiative. You will be trusted to make your voice heard and to deliver your best work.

The role is built for growth. You will deepen your expertise in cleaning validation and process qualification, strengthen your stakeholder management skills across departments, and learn from colleagues across API facilities while helping others develop.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

jobs.occupation: Manager - Software Engineering and Developer Tooling
jobs.description:
Denmark

Smørum

We are looking for a people leader for a mature, well-functioning team of 11 software engineers, split roughly equally between Smørum and Warsaw. You will help colleagues build confidence, use their strengths and grow in their careers through trust and honest feedback. You will be based in Smørum and travel to Warsaw up to six times a year.

The role

The team, called Toolbox, owns Gearbox, an essential tool for building, testing and producing our hearing aid products. Gearbox gives departments a common language and shared data abstractions, and it supports all the communication interfaces needed in development and production. It is data driven and works across product generations, programs and chipsets. Our users rely on Gearbox as a stable, validated tool that performs correctly and gives clear feedback on errors and completed requests.

Your main responsibility is the people in the team. You get to know each person, understand what motivates them and what helps them grow, and you coach rather than direct. Together with the Product Owner and the Scrum Master, you form the team's leadership team and share responsibility for its performance and wellbeing. The Product Owner sets direction and priorities, the Scrum Master supports how the team works, and you lead the people side.

Your main responsibilities

• Lead and develop 11 colleagues by coaching them, giving them ownership and helping them grow in a direction that fits both them and the team.

• Hold regular one-to-ones with each person about expectations, feedback, wellbeing and career development.

• Build the capabilities the team needs today and in the future through development, learning and recruitment, in line with product priorities and the technology strategy.

• Notice early when someone is struggling or losing motivation, and step in with support.

• Handle recruitment, compensation, budget and people processes together with your manager and People & Culture.

• Work as one leadership team with the Product Owner and Scrum Master on team health, learning and delivery.

• Understand the team's technical work and developer workflows well enough to remove obstacles for the team.

What you bring

You may already be a people leader, or you may be ready for your first line manager role. What matters most is the following:

• People first: You are motivated by helping others succeed and grow, and you give people trust and room to take ownership.

• Trust and feedback: You listen, build trust and give clear, honest feedback.

• Difficult conversations: You handle difficult conversations, including about performance, with fairness and respect.

• Leadership experience: You have led or developed others, for example as a manager, tech lead, Scrum Master or mentor.

• Technical understanding: You understand software engineering well enough to engage credibly with developers and architects, typically with a degree in engineering or computer science.

• Leading across sites: You can lead a team split between two locations and keep it working as one team.

Success in the role

After 12 to 18 months, you have earned a high level of trust from every member of the team, and you work closely with the Product Owner and the Scrum Master as one leadership team. Every team member has regular one-to-ones with you and a development plan they own and use. The team's engagement results are stable or improving, the team has kept its key people, and open positions are filled with the skills the team needs. Together with the Product Owner, you have an agreed plan for the skills the team needs over the next two years and how to build them. Colleagues in Smørum and Warsaw experience the same leadership and the same opportunities.

Development in the role: Over time, the role can grow into broader leadership, for example driving developer experience across the organisation or taking on a larger area as a senior manager.

Practical details

Workplace: Kongebakken, Smørum, Denmark (Global HQ)

Team: 11 people across Smørum and Warsaw

Travel: Warsaw up to six times per year

Application deadline: 27.11.26.

Hiring manager Jonas Funk Pedersen can be reached by email: jnfp@demant.com.

We screen and invite candidates on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

jobs.occupation: Advanced Product Development Engineer, Primary Packaging (12-month contact)
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Advanced Product Development Engineer within Primary Packaging, you will shape the primary packaging for Novo's next generation of pre-filled syringes. You will take ownership of technical areas, from new packaging systems to marketed products, working side by side with colleagues across drug and device development, production and supply chain. Your work helps treatments reach people living with serious chronic diseases safely and reliably.

What you’ll bring

You bring hands-on technical experience and enjoy turning design challenges into packaging that works in real life.

• An MSc or BSc in Engineering, Physics, Chemistry or another relevant natural science or technical field.

• Extensive experience in primary packaging for pharmaceutical products, or in medical device or combination product development. Technical depth and fit for the work matter most.

• Experience with requirements and specifications, verification, traceability and risk management in a regulated medical device or pharma environment (GMP/GxP/ISO).

• The ability to independently own a technical area, from assessment and decision to documentation and implementation in the product team and stakeholder landscape.

• Good stakeholder management skills.

• Fluent written and spoken English.

• A creative mindset, pride in delivering on your milestones, and energy for working across functions in a dynamic environment.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience with pre-filled syringes, syringes, cartridges, vials, stoppers or container closure systems, including Container Closure Integrity.

• Knowledge of how drugs and packaging materials interact, such as coatings, plastics, glues, silicone oil, and chemical and physical drug stability.

• Experience with ISO 15378, ISO 13485 and/or ISO 14971, or with systems engineering.

• Lifecycle management experience, including system ownership for marketed or late-stage products.

• Ability to provide technical direction, bring colleagues and stakeholders together, and drive technical activities towards successful delivery.

• Hands-on experience with technical drawings, tolerances and technical evaluation.

What you’ll do

You will help the team take on a wider portfolio of device projects, including new and larger pre-filled syringe formats and the lifecycle management of existing products.

• Develop primary packaging systems for parenteral administration, such as syringes and vials, from ideation to drug product launch.

• Bring in new primary packaging solutions, including ones not previously used at Novo, or insource existing solutions from external suppliers.

• Document design requirements, safety risk management, mitigations and testing, so that Clinical Trial Applications can be submitted.

• Ensure the right design, material, technical performance, processability and supply chain for each packaging system.

• Support marketed products through system ownership and late-stage changes.

• Scout the market, meet suppliers, and coordinate your own workstream with stakeholders to deliver on time.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Pre-Filled Syringe (PFS) Primary Packaging Development team in Drug Delivery Innovation, part of Global Manufacturing & Supply, based in Hillerød with state-of-the-art R&D facilities. The team brings together developers, specialists and project managers who focus on primary packaging for pre-filled syringes.

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain from drug and device development to marketed Novo products. Your closest partners will be colleagues in Drug and Device Development, Production and Supply Chain, along with project managers and external suppliers. They bring a constructive, collaborative mindset and offer highly competent sparring on your ideas.

Drug Delivery Innovation brings project management, engineering and technical functions together, so you will see how a diverse portfolio of drug, combination product and device projects comes together.

What you can expect here

You will work in a growing, international department where your expertise is valued and you are trusted to own your technical area. You will build new skills across drug and device development, production and supply chain, grow alongside experienced colleagues, and explore how packaging can contribute to a more circular economy.

This is a temporary position with a contract length of 1 year.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200 to 838,100 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to shape the primary packaging for the next generation of pre-filled syringes, apply for the Advanced Product Development Engineer, Primary Packaging role by 17 November 2026. Instead of a cover letter, add a few sentences about your motivation to your CV.

For further information, please contact Senior Manager, Frederik Yding Tingleff at FRHT@novonordisk.com.

Then you may be the intern we are looking for.

The position

Your responsibilities will include:

• Supporting monthly reporting and project controlling activities

• Contributing to monthly reporting across our project portfolio

• Supporting Power BI reporting and the continued development of management reports

• Following up on payments and supporting month-end controlling activities

• Helping document key financial processes and controlling standards

• Contributing to continuous improvement and new ways of working

The exact scope will develop with you. As you become familiar with the organisation and our ways of working, you will have opportunities to take greater ownership and support a broader range of activities.

Experience with Power BI would be an advantage. An interest in AI, technology and new digital ways of working would also be valuable.
